newsitem.title: JAPAN: Saudi term naphtha rise reflects good Asia demand.
newsitem.headline: Saudi term naphtha rise reflects good Asia demand.

text.p: Steep rises in Saudi Arabian term naphtha prices for Asian customers reflect expectations that the region's appetite for the petrochemical feedstock will grow rapidly, Tokyo traders said on Thursday.
Saudi Aramco, the state oil company of Saudi Arabia, is known for its tough negotiation skills, traders said.

However, they said Asian buyers accepted the substantial rise in prices for the first-half of calendar 1997, agreeing with the sellers' view that the supply and demand balance in Asia would tighten next year.
"Most people in the industry believe demand for naphtha will be good next year," a naphtha trader said.

In the price negotiations held in London last week, about a dozen importers, mostly from Japan and South Korea, accepted Aramco's offer to raise the premium of the naphtha grades mainly consumed in Asia by $2.50 to $3.10 per tonne.
Following the rise, the premium for the most popular A-180 naphtha, lifted at Ras Tanura on the Gulf coast, will be $6.50 above the Aramco formula for the first-half of 1997.
The new price compares with the current premium of $3.40 for the July to December period.
A-180 naphtha is paraffinic naphtha favoured among petrochemical firms as feedstock for ethylene production.
The premium for naphtha cargoes to be loaded at Jubail, also on the Gulf coast, was raised to $5.50 from $3.00.
Traders agreed that Asian demand for naphtha would rise, as a number of ethylene plants are scheduled to come on stream in the coming years as the region's economies expand.
Petrochemical Corp of Singapore, the city state's sole ethylene producer, plans to start operating a new plant, with annual production capacity of 515,000 tonnes, early next year.
The new facility will bring total output capacity there to 965,000 tonnes per year, according to the Japan Petrochemical Industry Association (JPCA).

Thailand's total ethylene production capacity is expected to grow by 350,000 tonnes a year to 1.1 million tonnes as Thai Petrochemical Industry Plc is planning to bring a new plant on line next year, a JPCA official said.
In South Korea, ethylene output capacity will be raised to about 4.3 million tonnes annually by the end of this year, compared with 3.95 million in 1995, the official said.
Ethylene plant expansion projects are also under way also in India and China, he added.
Another reason why Japanese term lifters accepted Aramco's offer is because there are no alternative suppliers that can provide the volume Saudi Arabia can, traders said.
Japan imported 20 million kilolitres (kl) of naphtha from January to August this year.
Saudi Arabia was the top supplier with 4.3 million kl, followed by Kuwait's 3.7 million kl and Singapore's two million kl.
